steps.title: Collect and freeze flatworms
steps.instruction: Gather 8 g (wet weight) of sexually mature flatworms that possess yolk glands, remove excess surface water without damaging tissue, and store at –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Prepare rearing water
steps.instruction: Autoclave tap water, let it cool to 20 °C, and use this as planarian rearing water.

steps.title: Prepare handling tools
steps.instruction: Obtain a soft paintbrush for shallow‑water work and a wide‑mouth (≈1 cm inner diameter) 10 mL glass pipette for deeper water; sterilize if desired and keep detergent‑free.

steps.title: Select and amputate large worms
steps.instruction: Choose asexual D. ryukyuensis worms ≥1 cm long, calculate the number needed (15 × X + 10 for the bioassay), and cut each into 2–3 equal fragments with a sharp razor blade.

substeps.instruction: Place a few worms on a 60 mm plastic Petri‑dish lid using the paintbrush.
For 1 cm worms cut in the middle (2 pieces); for longer worms cut at one‑third intervals (3 pieces).
When cutting into three pieces, make the first cut from the tail side to facilitate the second cut.

steps.title: Regenerate fragments for three weeks
steps.instruction: Transfer fragments to a Tupperware container filled with the 20 °C rearing water, change water 2–3 h after cutting, then change daily for the first 2 days and weekly thereafter; keep fragments on ice‑free water for 3 weeks without feeding.

substeps.instruction: Avoid damaging fragments; remove any pharynx that spits out to prevent water spoilage.
Maintain the container at 20 °C in an air‑conditioned room; no CO₂ or light cycle required.

steps.title: Select uniform 5–6 mm worms
steps.instruction: One day before the bioassay, pick 15 × X + 10 regenerated worms (5–6 mm long), discard the 10 smallest or largest to obtain 15 × X worms of uniform size, and divide them into X groups of 15 worms each.

substeps.instruction: Place selected worms in a single container for size comparison.
Remove the 10 outliers (smallest or largest).

steps.title: Perform feeding bioassay
steps.instruction: Feed each group of 15 OH‑strain planarians the test material (e.g., a few mm² of frozen flatworm tissue scraped with a knife) once daily; the food piece should be consumed within 7–10 min.

substeps.instruction: Keep OH strain at 20 °C; they never sexualize spontaneously.
Observe worms for sexual differentiation over the assay period.

steps.title: Label centrifuge tubes for extraction
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 mL conical tubes and label them as follows: 8 × “Homogenized”, 8 × “Supernatant 1st round”, 8 × “Supernatant 2nd round”, and 14 × “Ultra‑supernatant”.

steps.title: Homogenize flatworms (first round)
steps.instruction: Homogenize the 8 g frozen flatworms (1 g per tube) in 5 mL Milli‑Q water using a Potter‑type 10 mL homogenizer on ice, then bring each tube to 30 mL with additional water.

substeps.instruction: Keep samples on ice throughout.
Do not add protease inhibitors (the active compound is <500 Da and papain‑resistant).
Typical speed ≈3,000 rpm; ~4–5 s per stroke, ~25 strokes until no fragments are visible.

steps.title: Sonicate homogenate
steps.instruction: Sonicate each homogenized tube for 2 min 30 s while moving the tube evenly, using ≈30 % of the ultrasonic device’s maximum output (e.g., dial setting 3.5/11 on a UR‑200P).

substeps.instruction: Keep the tube on ice to prevent heating.
Avoid prolonged contact at one spot to prevent tube damage.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect 1st‑round supernatant
steps.instruction: Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C, balance tubes (add Milli‑Q water as needed), and spin at 16,000 g, 4 °C for 30 min; decant the supernatant into the “Supernatant 1st round” tubes.

substeps.instruction: Keep supernatant on ice after collection.

steps.title: Second‑round extraction on pellet
steps.instruction: Repeat homogenization, sonication, and centrifugation on the remaining pellet to recover additional activity.

substeps.instruction: Add ~3 mL Milli‑Q water to the pellet, float it with a spatula, and transfer to the homogenizer.
Add another 2 mL water to the original tube and collect any remaining pellet.
Homogenize the pellet in a total of 5 mL water (see step 9 for parameters).
Sonicate and centrifuge as before; collect the supernatant into the “Supernatant 2nd round” tubes.
Keep all samples on ice between steps.

steps.title: Filter extracts through 0.2 µm PES filter
steps.instruction: Pass the combined first‑ and second‑round supernatants (total ≈480 mL) through NALGENE Rapid‑Flow 0.2 µm PES filters; replace the filter when clogged.

substeps.instruction: If the rapid‑flow system is unavailable, a 10 mL syringe with a 0.22 µm PVDF filter can be used, though it is not recommended.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge filtered supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 15 mL of filtered supernatant into each ultracentrifuge tube, balance tubes with Milli‑Q water, and spin at 120,000 g, 4 °C for 40 min.

substeps.instruction: Place balanced tube pairs on the diagonal of the rotor.
Collect every drop of supernatant with a P1000 pipette into “Ultra‑supernatant” tubes.
With a 15 mL × 12‑tube rotor, the whole sample requires three runs, yielding ~14 “Ultra‑supernatant” tubes.

steps.title: Freeze ultra‑supernatant at –80 °C
steps.instruction: When ~30–40 mL of ultra‑supernatant has accumulated in a 50 mL tube, freeze the tube at –80 °C with a slight tilt to increase surface area; avoid insulating tube stands (e.g., Styrofoam).

substeps.instruction: Store frozen samples in a stable position in a deep freezer.
Samples retain activity for at least 6 months at –80 °C.

steps.title: Lyophilize frozen extract
steps.instruction: Place the tilted, frozen tubes in a freeze‑dryer, protect them from light with aluminium foil, and lyophilize until all solvent is removed, yielding a dry powder of the sex‑inducing substance.

substeps.instruction: Use a vented‑then‑vacuum‑state cycle as shown in the protocol figures.
